title: The Daily Me Versus the Daily Others: How Do Recommendation Algorithms Change User Interests? Evidence from a Knowledge-Sharing Platform
eligible_reason: Single intervention date applied to all users simultaneously; RDiT time-series design with time-varying controls and polynomial trends, not a unit/time TWFE.
design_notes: Regression discontinuity in time (RDiT) around one platform-wide intervention: Zhihu switched from content-based to social-filtering recommendation around noon on Aug 16, 2012. Eq. 1: ln(Y_jt) = a + b After_t + polynomial in t (order chosen by BIC) interacted with After_t + day-of-week and month FE + ln new users and ln new topics, on daily platform-level counts in a 30-day window (Tables 1-4). User-segment and topic-segment tables aggregate users or topics to segment-day series and re-run the same RDiT. No staggered adoption, no unit-level panel with unit FE in the main results, time-varying controls and flexible time polynomials.
screener_notes: Not eligible: RDiT, one date. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Zhihu internal data sets provided to the authors under cooperation (not public).
